formalization_review.reason: The iter-012 redraft re-signed the drive but did not re-sign the lumped-law/heat-current coupling, leaving both value theorems semantically broken. (1) acrylicConductivity_officialSample is refuted by an explicit countermodel: h = 1, H_Th = 0.2629 satisfies 0 < h, 0 < H_Th and 0.2629 <= h*H_Th, but hformula then gives lam = ln(465/337)/(2*pi*0.2629) ~= 0.1949, so |lam - 0.25| ~= 0.0551 > 0.01. First-hand recomputation: ln(23.25/16.85) = 0.321954, and |lam-0.25| <= 0.01 holds iff h*H_Th in [0.19708, 0.21350]; every premise value >= 0.2629 lies strictly outside the band. The threshold 0.2629 is on the wrong side; the chapter's own certified arithmetic (lam <= 0.3220/(6.2831*0.2629) < 0.195) proves the negation of the conclusion, not the conclusion. (2) acrylicConductivity_formula's hypothesis bundle is unsatisfiable over Lean's reals, so the theorem holds only vacuously: P0 := P r1 = (T_OC - T_IC)/R_Th < 0 (hflow, hR, hDeltaT), steady makes P = P0 on [r1,r2], and fourier then forces deriv T r = -P0/(lam*2*pi*r*h) > 0 at every wall radius (non-junk: deriv T r = 0 would violate fourier since P0 != 0, hence T is differentiable, thus continuous, throughout [r1,r2]); MVT on [r1,r2] then yields T r2 > T r1, i.e. T_OC > T_IC, contradicting hDeltaT : T_OC < T_IC. Root cause: Eq. (4)'s P is the heat INTO the IC (an inward current when the IC gains heat), while RadialFourierConduction's P is the outward wall current; with the repaired drive T_OC < T_IC (IC hot, heat flowing outward IC -> OC) the lumped heat received by the IC is -P r1, so hflow must read LumpedHeatFlowLaw D (-P G.r1) (equivalently Eq. (4) as T_IC - T_OC over R_Th, or the reversed drive T_IC < T_OC whose Cauchy-Bunyakovsky countermodel refuted iter-010). The derivation route now described in the file's own docstring (FTC identity T_OC - T_IC = -P0*ln(r2/r1)/(2 pi lam h), cancel d != 0) yields 1 = -ln(r2/r1)/(2 pi lam h R_Th) < 0, i.e. it refutes the hypothesis bundle instead of deriving the formula.

countermodel_resistance.evidence: Both theorems fail constructively. Sample theorem: h = 1, H_Th = 0.2629, lam = ln(23.25e-3/16.85e-3)/(2*pi*1*0.2629) satisfies all four premises (0 < 1, 0 < 0.2629, hformula by definition, 0.2629 <= 1*0.2629) yet |lam - 0.25| ~= 0.0551 > 0.01 - verified numerically first-hand (ln ratio = 0.3219544752349946). Formula theorem: the hypothesis bundle is unsatisfiable - if (G, D, lam, T, P) satisfied hflow, hfourier, 0 < R_Th, 0 < lam, boundary conditions and T_OC < T_IC, then P0 = (T_OC-T_IC)/R_Th < 0, steady gives P = P0 on [r1,r2], fourier gives deriv T r = -P0/(2*pi*lam*h*r) > 0 at every r in [r1,r2] (and T is differentiable there since deriv T r = 0 would force P r = 0 != P0), so MeanValue.deriv_eq_slope (or MVT) on [r1,r2] yields some c with deriv T c = (T_OC-T_IC)/(r2-r1) < 0, contradiction. A theorem whose premises admit no model is vacuous and cannot serve as the C.7 derivation carrier.
